summary: Benton County lookout: a 60-foot tower in operation by February 1950, staffed by Ted Edwards, with a new steel tower erected in FY 1970-71. No source gives its current state.

events.note: 4-acre towersite acquired; the page dates this to fiscal 1948-49
Ted Edwards started with the Commission in November 1949 and was assigned the Lincoln towerman post (obituary)
60-foot lookout tower built and in operation by February 1950, per a Sedalia Democrat report; the page gives no construction date
Obituary of towerman Ted Edwards, who had served at Lincoln for the past nine years; he died August 26, 1958. This is the last named towerman in our sources
new steel tower erected at Lincoln in FY 1970-71; the page does not say whether the 1950 tower came down and gives no height for the steel tower

evidence.supports: Missouri Conservation Commission agency and Benton County listing
evidence.quote: Missouri Lookouts - Benton County - Missouri Conservation Commission - 41N-21W-6
FY 1948-49: A 4 acre towersite was acquired.

evidence.supports: 60-foot lookout tower built and in operation by February 1950; Ted Edwards of Warsaw in charge
evidence.quote: A 60 foot lookout tower for the purpose of protection against forest fires has been constructed and is now in operation with Ted Edwards of Warsaw in charge.

evidence.supports: second such tower in Benton County, about four miles southeast on the Lakeview Heights road
evidence.quote: It is the second such tower to be constructed in Benton county and is located about four miles southeast of here on the Lakeview Heights road.

evidence.supports: towermen furnished a jeep with firefighting gear, including a 180-gallon water tank and pump
evidence.quote: A jeep with firefighting equipment including a 180 gallon water tank and pump is furnished to each tower man.

evidence.supports: the seasons of greatest danger were early spring and the autumn and winter months (November and December)
evidence.quote: It is said the greatest danger from forest fires is during the early spring and the autumn and winter months of November and December.

evidence.supports: towermen at their posts day and night in those seasons
evidence.quote: For this reason tower men will be at their posts 24 hours a day at these particular seasons.

evidence.supports: radio linked the tower to others, headquarters at Camdenton
evidence.quote: Radio equipment has been installed with direct contact to other towers, headquarters being at Camdenton.

evidence.supports: running costs from fishing and hunting license sales
evidence.quote: Funds with which to meet expenses of the tower will be obtained from the sale of fishing and hunting licenses.

evidence.supports: views from the windows: Lincoln, Ionia, Cole Camp and Stover
evidence.quote: From the lookout windows are towns of Lincoln, Ionia, Cole Camp and Stover can be observed.

evidence.supports: Ted Edwards started November 1949 and was assigned to the Lincoln tower
evidence.quote: Edwards started to work for the Conservation Commission in November, 1949, and was assigned the position of towerman at Lincoln lookout tower, in Benton county.

evidence.supports: Edwards died at his home in Warsaw, August 26 (1958), after a lingering illness; age 51
evidence.quote: Ted Edwards, 51, forest towerman for the Conservation Commission, died at his home in Warsaw August 26 following a lingering illness.

evidence.supports: he had served at Lincoln for the past nine years
evidence.quote: He served in that capacity for the past nine years.

evidence.supports: new steel tower erected at Lincoln, FY 1970-71
evidence.quote: A new steel tower was erected at Lincoln.

notes_for_editor: One source: the Central US Lookouts Lincoln page. It quotes a FY 1948-49 state annual report, a February 1950 Sedalia Democrat report, a September 1958 obituary from The Index, and a FY 1970-71 annual report. None of the originals was checked. Web search was not available in this run (the shared budget was used up before this tower was reached), so no newspaper archive, MDC history or heritage page was checked. Current status, access and whether the 1950 tower came down are unknown; no source goes past FY 1970-71. Staffing is 'staffed' as of 1958, the last named towerman; the obituary implies he held the post until he died, so staffed_last 1958 is an inference from that. No height_m is set: the 60-foot figure belongs to the 1950 tower and the steel tower has no height in the sources. The brief's record (lat/lon, county, agency) matches the page. The 1950 quote says 'four miles southeast of here'; the story does not name an anchor point because the page does not say what 'here' is.
